name: MILK10k: Multimodal Imaging-Learning Toolkit for Skin Cancer
description: MILK10k (Multimodal Imaging-Learning Toolkit for Diagnosing Pigmented and Nonpigmented Skin Cancer and its Simulators) is a curated dermatological dataset compiled by researchers from the Medical University of Vienna and the International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC), published in the Journal of Investigative Dermatology. Hosted on the ISIC Archive (DOI: 10.34970/648456), MILK10k comprises 10,480 images representing 5,240 skin lesions from international clinical centers (Austria, Turkey, the US, Australia, North Macedonia). For every lesion, the dataset pairs a clinical close-up photograph with a polarized dermoscopic image. Over 95.7% of lesions are histopathologically confirmed, providing balanced coverage of pigmented and non-pigmented skin cancers and benign simulators across 11 diagnostic categories (AKIEC, BCC, BKL, DF, INF, MEL, NV, SCCKA, VASC, BEN_OTH, MAL_OTH). Images are further annotated with concept terms (pigmentation, erythema, ulceration, vessels) and Fitzpatrick-aligned skin tone clusters (levels 0–5).
